key_insight: Error-Conditioned Neural Solvers learn to correct their own mistakes instead of treating PDE solving as a one-shot prediction problem. This makes neural surrogates more physically consistent and more robust outside the training distribution, while avoiding the heavy cost of iterative classical optimization.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a key limitation of neural surrogate models for PDEs: they are fast but often violate physical constraints and fail to self-correct when predictions are inaccurate or when inputs fall outside the training range.
method: Condition the solver on its current prediction error so the model can learn how to refine bad outputs.
Combine neural surrogate speed with an error-correction mechanism that reduces PDE residuals without relying on expensive gradient-descent or Gauss-Newton iterations.
Aim to improve both physical consistency and out-of-distribution generalization compared with standard surrogate and hybrid solver approaches.
impact: For ML practitioners, this offers a path to faster PDE solving with better reliability and fewer constraint violations. It is especially useful when classical iterative solvers are too slow or unstable, but pure neural surrogates are not accurate enough.
